Executive Findings & Synthesis

1. The Value of Multimodal Signals

Adding 84 facial Action Units and eye gaze vectors (view_physio_face) produced the absolute highest performance across the entire benchmark, boosting Macro F1 to 0.6698 (+3.95% over physio alone) and ROC AUC to 0.7022.

2. Classical vs Deep on Stationary Windows

On 60-second calibrated physiological windows, tree-based models (Random Forest: 0.6303, XGBoost: 0.6230) outperform recurrent sequence backpropagation (CNN-GRU: 0.5962) due to tree ensembles' sample efficiency on stationary tabular features.

3. Adversarial GRL Regularization

While un-regularized deep models required shifting decision boundaries down to 0.10–0.35, the Adversarial GRL head (λ=0.02) suppressed subject identity, improved accuracy to 62.55%, and stabilized the optimal threshold exactly at 0.50.

Deep Learning & Adversarial GRL Analysis

1. Why Tabular Random Forest Outperforms Plain Deep Models

In alignment with the EDA's within-task dynamics finding (Section 4), calibrated physiological features are summarized over 60s windows. Because intra-window dynamics remain stationary around zero, gradient-boosted decision trees and ensemble Random Forests (Macro F1 = 0.6303) exploit high-dimensional nonlinear threshold interactions more effectively than recurrent backpropagation on moderate sample sizes (N=1,394).

2. Impact of Adversarial Identity Suppression (λ=0.02)

Adding a Gradient Reversal Layer with a 63-subject identification head forces the 1D-CNN + GRU backbone to learn representations that are invariant to individual physiological baselines. This improved accuracy from 61.26% to 62.55% and stabilized the optimal decision threshold exactly at 0.50, eliminating the threshold shift required by un-regularized models.

// PyTorch GRL Multi-Task Loss Formulation
loss_stress = CrossEntropyLoss(stress_logits, y_true, weight=[1.0, 1.71])
rep_reversed = GradReverse(representation, lambda_adv=0.02)
subject_logits = SubjectClassifier(rep_reversed)
loss_subject = CrossEntropyLoss(subject_logits, subject_id)
total_loss = loss_stress + loss_subject

Backward Pass:
dL/d(rep) = dL_stress/d(rep) - 0.02 * dL_subject/d(rep)
// Gradient reversal forces feature extractor to confuse subject identity
